title: Write: External Memory
subtitle: Persisting context outside the window — scratchpads, structured notes, and curated files the model reads back on demand
topics: The write family: save context outside the window, read back only what the task needs [LC-WSCI]
Structured note-taking (agentic memory): decisions, open issues, and identifiers — not transcripts [ANTHROPIC-CE]
The app's notes mode: session notes replace raw history on every subsequent ask
Curated write artifacts beyond the session: canonical concept files and project context files
The write trade: an upkeep cost per turn buys a shrinking history layer forever

analogy.title: The Ward Nurse's Handover Sheet
analogy.text: A hospital shift change does not replay the last twelve hours of hallway conversation to the incoming nurse. The outgoing nurse maintains a handover sheet — patient, status, meds given, watch-for — updated as events happen, structured the same way every shift. Twelve hours of noise become one sheet of load-bearing facts; the incoming nurse reads it in two minutes and asks about anything unclear. Notes mode is the handover sheet; naive history is making the new nurse listen to the hallway tape.

antiPatterns: Transcript hoarding disguised as memory: 'notes' that are just pasted conversation chunks — same tokens, new label, no structure to read back selectively
Write-only memory: notes accumulate forever and are never pruned or read back — the sheet becomes a second history layer with worse formatting
Unstructured prose notes: without fixed fields (decision, open issue, identifier), the reader model has to re-derive what mattered — spending the tokens the notes were meant to save

sections.title: The Write Family, Precisely
sections.body:
Write means saving context outside the window so it doesn't ride along on every call ([LC-WSCI]). Anthropic's guidance names the discipline structured note-taking — agentic memory that persists decisions, unresolved issues, and critical identifiers rather than transcripts, retrieved later to maintain coherence across long work ([ANTHROPIC-CE]).

The key word is structured. A note like PA-1002 | MANUAL_REVIEW | missing: C-72148-2 | reviewer asked about EMG timing costs ~20 tokens and answers three future questions. The same information buried in four turns of chat costs hundreds and answers nothing until re-read in full. Write is a trade with two sides: you pay a small upkeep cost at write time (deciding what's load-bearing, appending the note) and collect on every subsequent call whose history layer would otherwise have grown.

sections.title: Notes Mode on the Receipt
sections.body:
Flip MedFlow to notes and ask a few questions in one session. After each answer the backend appends structured notes to a session store; every subsequent ask loads the notes and drops raw history. On the receipt: the history layer collapses, a small retrieved-notes line appears, and Q9 — the member-history summary that naive answers for 1,700 tokens — bills 167 tokens, PASS (replay grid, synthetic-pre-recording). Across the whole question set, notes medians 198 tokens at 100% correctness — the second-cheapest mode in the grid, and the cheapest on aggregation questions, because aggregations are exactly what good notes pre-compute.

Beyond the session, the write family scales into curated artifacts: canonical concept files that settle a fact once (U05 meets them as okf mode), and project context files like CLAUDE.md that orient every future session. The parent graph course measured both at repository scale — its OKF bundles and layered-CLAUDE.md arms are this family industrialized (KG M06–M08). The kit's memory track (M12–M15) covers the session-to-persistent ladder in depth (context-eng-kit).

sections.question: WHEN does notes mode beat compressed history summarization for a long review session?
options: B. When the session has identifiable milestones and load-bearing identifiers: notes capture them at write time with zero loss, while summarization must re-decide what mattered after the fact and can drop a fact it didn't know was load-bearing
C. When the model is small
D. Only when caching is off
sections.explanation: Task-context alignment [ANTHROPIC-CE]: note-taking fits iterative work with milestones. Compression decides retroactively what mattered; structured writes decide at the moment of knowing — which is why compressed dropped PA-1004 on Q9 and notes didn't.

sections.question: Your notes store has grown to 3,000 tokens after a week of sessions and every ask now ships all of it. WHY has write stopped working?
options: A. Notes were a bad idea for this workload

B. The store violated write's second half: persistence without selective read-back just relocated the history problem — notes need structure and retrieval (read back only what this ask touches), or pruning tied to resolved issues
C. The model's window is too small
D. It hasn't stopped working — 3,000 tokens is fine
sections.explanation: Write = save outside AND read back selectively. A monotonically growing, fully-shipped store is the write-only anti-pattern — the handover sheet has become the hallway tape.

sections.title: What Goes Wrong
items: The eternal scratchpad: no pruning rule, so week-old resolved issues ride into every call — notes need a lifecycle (open → resolved → archived), not just an append
Notes without identifiers: 'discussed the MRI request' instead of 'PA-1002' — un-look-up-able, un-gradeable, and the first thing a future answer will get wrong
Trusting notes you never audit: a wrong fact written once is repeated forever with the confidence of memory — graded questions (the stamp) are how a wrong note gets caught

takeaway: Write context out of the window as structured, identifier-bearing notes at the moment of knowing — and read back selectively, or you've only renamed the history problem.
labUnderstand: Run a three-question session in naive mode and the same session in notes mode; watch the history layer collapse on the receipts and the session sparkline flatten, then inspect the note store and find the exact line that answered Q9 for 167 tokens.
labBuild: Have Claude write a session-notes evaluator: replay a scripted five-ask session in notes mode, extract the note store, and assert every load-bearing identifier (PA-1001, PA-1004, statuses) survived into notes while total session input stayed under a budget.
